meta.name: ACF Glossary
meta.purpose: Single source of truth for inline tooltip content across all six framework parts and for the /glossary reference index, which is GENERATED from this file (scripts/build-glossary-page.mjs). Tooltips and the index are populated from this file; never hand-author a second glossary.

schema.id: stable slug, used as the data key and tooltip anchor (kebab-case)
schema.aliases: alternate spellings/phrasings the tagger should also match
schema.wave: 1 = first rollout pass (highest comprehension value), 2 = second pass
schema.category: closed key from meta.categories; groups the /glossary index (explicit, never derived from appearsLater)
schema.definition: layer-one tooltip copy: concise, plain-English, no em dashes
schema.length: short | medium — sizing hint for the tooltip card

source.ref: internal -> own Part; external -> primary/academic citation

schema.related: layer-two: sibling concept ids whose roots should wake on hover (the mycelium adjacency)
schema.appearsLater: layer-two: the part where this term becomes operational ('see where this appears later')
schema.chart: id of the chart in the chart-handoff inventory that substantiates this term, if any

meta.usage: Tooltip layer one shows 'definition'. Layer two ('see where this appears later') is built from 'appearsLater' + 'related'. The 'related' and 'chart' ids share vocabulary with the chart-handoff CONNECTS-TO network so the glossary and the charts form one cross-reference graph. Internal sources cite the framework's own Parts; external sources cite primary/academic references.
meta.harmonizeNote: Carry vectors harmonized 2026-07-26: defined at first use in the Part 1 abstract, sourced to the product's closed structure enum (Long Carry | Short Carry | Barbell), and cross-linked to carry direction inside the CIS macro component (Part 6). Power-law corridor was harmonized against Part 3 earlier.

terms.definition: Exposure where the upside can compound far faster than the downside, so being right pays off disproportionately more than being wrong costs.

source.ref: Part 1 — Foundation & Philosophy; scored in Part 6

appearsLater.topic: How convexity is expressed through Posture

terms.definition: Convexity Integrity Score: a 0 to 100 score rating one position at a time on convexity and optionality, risk and fragility, macro alignment, and execution and sentiment.
A probabilistic read of the current regime that sets the portfolio's structure. It is a framing device, not a point forecast.

appearsLater.topic: The lineage and the full regime thesis

terms.definition: A predefined threshold that forces review or action before denial, emotion, or information overload can take over.

source.ref: Part 1 order of operations; operational in Part 5

terms.definition: A trend-validation rule: the framework checks that the market is confirming the thesis before it allows a full position size.

source.ref: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012); Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), trend-following evidence

terms.definition: The legal account container (Roth, taxable, or pre-tax) whose tax rules materially change long-run compounding outcomes.

source.ref: Part 4 — Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; external IRS Pubs 590-A / 590-B

terms.definition: Controlled convexity: high-upside exposure to durable, real regime forces that can tolerate serious drawdowns.
Capital-preserving reserve and rotation capital that helps the portfolio survive stress and buy into dislocations.
Narrative-driven convexity with weak structural backing. Useful only with strict limits and automatic exits.

appearsLater.topic: The Hype posture and its limits

terms.definition: A condition where public debt and financing constraints begin to dictate what monetary policy can realistically do.

source.ref: Part 1 tripwire language; external fiscal-dominance literature (Federal Reserve Board)

appearsLater.topic: The macro thesis and policy backdrop

terms.definition: Borrowing against appreciated assets instead of selling them, potentially deferring realization. It depends on current law and financing availability.
Vulnerability to disorder and nonlinear shocks, not just price movement. A fragile position breaks when stress rises.

source.ref: Taleb & Douady (2012), Mathematical Definition, Mapping, and Detection of (Anti)Fragility

terms.definition: The behavioral classification every non-Bitcoin position carries: Torque, Ballast, or Hype. It sets the position's sizing bands and governance rules; behavior, not asset type, is what the framework classifies. Bitcoin sits outside all three, governed by Part 3.
Markets react to policy and policymakers react back to markets, creating feedback loops that can amplify instability.
High-volatility periods tend to arrive in clusters rather than as isolated events, which changes how risk should be managed.

appearsLater.topic: The traditional playbook is failing quietly

terms.definition: Correlations between assets are regime-dependent and can flip when inflation or liquidity stress dominates.

source.ref: BIS (2023), The correlation of equity and bond returns

terms.definition: Building a portfolio that can stay alive through timing errors, volatility, and thesis delays while keeping exposure to large upside.
Rare but very large gains that dominate total portfolio outcomes, which is why their tax treatment matters so much.
An AI-assisted research loop that speeds evidence-gathering once a tripwire fires, without handing final judgment to the machine.
Total Addressable Market: a deliberately conservative estimate of the capital a market could absorb over time, used to size an asset's potential rather than to forecast a price.

appearsLater.topic: The conservative addressable-market estimate for the Bitcoin reserve

terms.definition: A long-run regression channel, on a log scale, that Bitcoin's price has historically tracked. The framework reads it as a context band for accumulation pace, not a deterministic price prediction.

source.ref: Part 3 — Bitcoin: Convexity Backbone; external power-law model (Santostasi)

terms.definition: The risk that the order of gains and losses, not just their average, determines whether a portfolio survives. A large drawdown at the wrong time can permanently impair compounding.
A structure that pairs very safe holdings with a small, highly convex allocation and skips the fragile middle. It targets payoff asymmetry, not low volatility.

source.ref: Taleb, barbell strategy; internal Part 2 lineage

terms.definition: Buying a fixed amount on a set schedule regardless of price, which spreads entry risk across time. The framework funds it from income and accelerates it into deep drawdowns.
Reserve cash kept ready to deploy into dislocations. The framework builds it during extensions and spends it when valuations converge on undervaluation.

A distribution treated as a return of your own invested capital rather than taxable income. It reduces cost basis and defers tax rather than eliminating it; classification can change and depends on current law.

Framework Integrity Score: a 0 to 100 portfolio-construction score that starts the assembled portfolio at 100 and deducts a named penalty for each rule violation, so every lost point is attributable and repairable.

The framework's closed structure classification for a position: Long Carry, Short Carry, or Barbell. In CIS scoring, carry direction measures whether a position benefits from or suffers under the current rate and inflation regime; a barbell pairs the two exposures.

source.ref: Part 1 abstract (carry vectors, after Park's carry framework); CIS Spec v2.1 §5.2 (carry direction); product structure registry (closed enum)

appearsLater.topic: Carry direction inside the CIS macro component

terms.definition: An account funded with after-tax dollars where qualified withdrawals are not taxed, so appreciation compounds and trades without tax friction. The framework treats its annual capacity as scarce and reserves it for positions that may be rotated.

An ordinary investment account with no contribution limit, where realized gains and distributions are taxed in the year they occur. The framework routes never-sold and income-producing holdings here, including the Bitcoin backbone.

An account funded before tax where contributions reduce current income and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income. The framework treats it as tactical rather than structural, because the deferred tax obligation compounds alongside the balance.

Reaching Roth treatment above the direct income limits by contributing to a traditional IRA and converting. It preserves access under current law and is subject to the pro-rata rule when other pre-tax balances exist.

A withdrawal the law compels from pre-tax accounts starting at age 73, rising to 75 in 2033 under current rules. It forces taxable income regardless of need, which is one reason the framework prefers Roth for long-horizon convexity.

source.ref: Part 4 — Tax Architecture & ROC Strategy; external IRS Pub 590-B

terms.definition: An additional 3.8 percent federal tax on investment income above certain income thresholds. It is part of why a taxable account retains materially less of a large gain than a Roth.

The taxable profit realized when an appreciated position is sold. Long-held positions generally receive preferential rates, which is why holding period and wrapper placement change what a gain is worth.
What a position is treated as having cost for tax purposes. Gains are measured against it, return-of-capital distributions reduce it, and under current law it may reset at death.

The reset of an inherited asset's cost basis to its value at death under current law, which can erase the embedded gain. It is policy-dependent and not guaranteed, and it underpins the never-sell treatment of the Bitcoin backbone.

Realizing a loss deliberately to offset gains, or a limited amount of ordinary income, while keeping the exposure through a non-identical position. The harvested loss carries forward as a durable tax asset.
A rule that disallows a realized loss when a substantially identical position is repurchased inside a set window. It is why harvesting redeploys into a similar but not identical holding.
Taking a deduction at a high marginal rate in one year and converting the balance to Roth in a later, lower-rate year. The captured value is the spread between the two rates.
What the portfolio is actually worth at the end of the horizon, after every tax, fee, and friction has been paid. The framework optimizes for it rather than for any single year's return.

appearsLater.topic: Wrapper engineering as a structural edge

terms.definition: How much capital a single position is allowed to carry. In this framework size is earned: the score selects a band, the posture scales it, and concentration limits cap it at the household level.

The target size range a score maps into for a given posture. Seventy and above supports core sizing, sixty to sixty-nine constrained, fifty to fifty-nine starter, and below fifty is not allocation-worthy.

A ceiling on how much any single name or small group may represent, applied to the household aggregate across every account. Fifteen percent is the default single-position cap, eighteen percent the absolute with a documented override.
A decline from a position's or portfolio's recent peak. The framework treats a survivable drawdown as the price of convexity rather than as a malfunction, provided reserves make it holdable.
How much a price moves. The framework separates it from fragility: a position can be highly volatile and still robust, and the difference is whether the move threatens survival.

Whether a position or portfolio can withstand stress without being forced into a decision that ends the compounding. It is scored inside CIS as Risk and Fragility, where a higher score means lower fragility.

Moving capital between postures as conditions change, most often trimming Ballast after Torque runs and redeploying into Torque during dislocations. It is the framework's primary way of buying low without raising outside cash.
An exit level committed to before entry. Hype positions carry them by doctrine, and the framework forbids widening a stop or reclassifying a position to avoid honoring one.

The protocol governing exposure around a scheduled earnings date. A position entering the final five trading days is capped at three percent of portfolio value, because the event is binary and conviction does not predict it.

appearsLater.topic: Earnings proximity: cap the binary event

terms.definition: A durable structural driver that capital must flow toward, identified in the macro thesis. The framework allocates by force rather than by sector, and diversifies across several expressions of the same force.

appearsLater.topic: Allocate by force, not by sector

terms.definition: The highest price of the past year, used as the reference for absolute momentum. Distance below it grades a position from healthy, through correction, to severe distress.
How widely a move is shared across related names. Broad participation supports a thesis; narrowing leadership warns that a move is thinning even while the index holds.
Borrowing against portfolio assets rather than selling them. The framework treats it as an optional overlay, revocable by the broker and repriceable under stress, never as a structural requirement.

A conscious, documented, time-bounded deviation from a default parameter, carrying the reasoning and the conditions under which it reverts. An unexamined drift is not an override; it is the framework being abandoned quietly.
The non-negotiable layer of the framework: the principles that define what it is. Changing one means no longer implementing the framework, as distinct from tuning a parameter or logging an override.
The strength of the evidence behind a position, as opposed to enthusiasm for it. The framework quantifies it through CIS so that size follows demonstrated evidence rather than feeling.
The prevailing structural conditions that determine how assets behave and correlate. The framework is built to adapt when the regime changes rather than to optimize for the average of all regimes.
Holding a position whose future paths include large upside without committing to which one occurs. It is the property CIS scores first, because it is what convexity is made of.
A payoff where the upside and downside are unequal in size or probability. The framework seeks it deliberately and treats symmetric risk measures as an incomplete description of survival.

The shared four-level register both scores read: seventy and above Strong, sixty to sixty-nine Moderate, fifty to fifty-nine Caution, below fifty Weak. On FIS seventy is also the action line; on CIS it is a band boundary, not an action trigger.

A cap on how far a score may move in a single update, scaled by how good the underlying evidence is. It forces a large re-rating to be earned across successive updates rather than granted in one enthusiastic week.
How much the evidence behind a score can support, derived by the engine from the quality of each source rather than asserted by hand. It sets how far a single update is allowed to move the score.
The structural class a position belongs to, which selects the lens CIS scores it through. It changes how the rubric is applied, never what the final number is floored at.

Starting a portfolio at one hundred and deducting a named penalty for each rule violation. Every point below one hundred is attributable to a specific departure, so the score reads as a repair list rather than a verdict.
The itemized account of which rule cost how many points. It is what makes a construction score actionable, because the fix is named alongside the deduction.
Capital held without a documented thesis or on a score nobody has refreshed. It is one of the five FIS penalty buckets, and it scales with position size.

Scaling a penalty by how large the offending position is, within a floor and a cap. A bigger position generates a proportionally bigger charge, but no single position is allowed to dominate the score.

The gap between the portfolio's actual posture mix and its target, which the market can open without a single trade. It is reported as a diagnostic alongside the score rather than billed as a penalty.
The record of what changed, why, and what would reverse it, written as the weekly loop closes. It is what makes the next week's pass a measurement rather than a memory.

Holding a deteriorating position because the story still sounds right. The framework names it as a failure mode of traditional portfolio management and answers it with quantified reassessment, so evidence rather than narrative decides whether a position stays.

source.ref: Part 1 — the failure modes the architecture addresses

appearsLater.topic: The failure modes the system answers

terms.definition: Missing a thesis break because there is more information than attention. The framework answers it with tripwires, which automate attention to the critical signals so a break is noticed when it happens rather than when it becomes convenient.

source.ref: Part 1 — the failure modes the architecture addresses

appearsLater.topic: The failure modes the system answers

terms.definition: The chance of a loss large enough to end compounding, which no later gain can repair. The framework treats ruin as a boundary condition rather than a risk to be traded off: survival comes first, because nothing compounds from zero.

source.ref: Taleb, Antifragile and The Black Swan; internal Part 2 lineage

terms.definition: The aggregate supply of money and credit in the system, read through measures such as M2 growth, central-bank balance sheets, and real rates. The framework treats its expansion and contraction as a tide that convex assets amplify rather than merely follow.

source.ref: Lyn Alden, liquidity-cycle work; internal Part 2 lineage

terms.definition: The reserve asset and principal source of convexity: a Bitcoin position held outside the three postures, accumulated on a schedule, governed by valuation discipline, and never sold, traded, or rebalanced. Liquidity comes from elsewhere.

source.ref: Part 3 — Bitcoin as the convexity backbone

terms.definition: Holding the Bitcoin reserve in hardware wallets under the holder’s own keys, accumulated through payroll contributions and held rather than trimmed on valuation. A custodian enters only if and when collateralized borrowing begins.

source.ref: Part 3 — TAM, custody, and the borrow phase

appearsLater.topic: Cold-storage architecture and the borrow phase

terms.definition: The handling rule for the backbone: Bitcoin is accumulated and never sold, traded, or rebalanced. Valuation models shape the pace of buying, not entries and exits, and cash needs are met from income, other assets, or borrowing against the reserve.

source.ref: Part 3 — Handling doctrine: accumulate, then borrow

terms.definition: The valuation read for Bitcoin: several independent models are compared, and their agreement is the signal. Convergence on undervaluation accelerates accumulation, convergence on overvaluation slows it, and wide divergence counsels holding the range.

source.ref: Part 3 — Why Bitcoin can be modeled

terms.definition: Bitcoin’s aggregate on-chain cost basis, with each coin valued at the price it last moved. It rises with adoption and marks a historically important bear-market regime level, not a hard floor: price can trade below it for extended stretches.

source.ref: Part 3 — Why Bitcoin can be modeled

terms.definition: Bitcoin’s share of the whole portfolio. A ten to fifteen percent target suits long horizons and moderate risk capacity, twenty to thirty percent suits higher conviction, and a mature thirty to fifty percent share can emerge over decades through accumulation rather than rebalancing.

source.ref: Part 3 — Reserve sizing by horizon and risk capacity

appearsLater.topic: Reserve sizing by horizon and risk capacity

terms.definition: A stretch in which Bitcoin trades well above its power-law trend and its realized-price basis. The response is to slow discretionary accumulation and build dry powder from income; an extension never prompts a sale of the reserve.

appearsLater.topic: Through two cycles: extension and convergence

terms.definition: The gap between a gross gain and what a given wrapper lets you keep after tax. It widens as the outcome grows, which is why the largest wins are the ones where wrapper placement matters most.

The only options use permitted inside a Roth: long calls, long puts, and defined-risk spreads, never undefined-risk strategies such as naked options or short volatility. A tactical overlay for a high-conviction thesis, capped at three to five percent of the account measured as maximum loss at entry.

appearsLater.topic: Options within the Roth: purchased convexity only

terms.definition: The portfolio boundary for every concentration rule: the total across all wrappers, including Roth, pre-tax, taxable, and Bitcoin cold storage. A position held in several accounts sums to one exposure, and the limits apply to that sum rather than to any single account.

source.ref: Part 5 — The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

appearsLater.topic: The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

terms.definition: A wrapper intentionally concentrated in one position, permitted only while the household aggregate stays inside its limits. The designation is explicit and documented, drift is monitored, and trimming is required if the aggregate breaches a cap. A governance structure, not an exception.

source.ref: Part 5 — The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

appearsLater.topic: The portfolio boundary and single-name sleeves

terms.definition: The truth problem, as distinct from the price problem: a core assertion behind a position has broken. Reassessment is immediate and price is irrelevant; a thesis-damaged position is downgraded or exited, and a later price recovery does not rehabilitate it.

source.ref: Part 5 — Thesis drift: price problems versus truth problems

appearsLater.topic: Thesis drift: price problems versus truth problems

terms.definition: The one to three claims a position depends on, written down at entry in a form that can be checked. They are what thesis drift is measured against: when one breaks, the position is reassessed on the evidence, whatever the price is doing.

source.ref: Part 5 — Protocol 05: one to three core assertions per position

appearsLater.topic: Protocol 05: one to three core assertions per position

terms.definition: A rule on the way in: a position down twenty percent or more from cost basis takes no new capital until a confirming signal arrives, such as a higher low, a reclaimed level, or new thesis-supporting evidence. Scaling in happens over weeks, with no more than a quarter of the target added in any one week.

source.ref: Part 5 — Adds and freezes: discipline on the way in

appearsLater.topic: Adds and freezes: discipline on the way in

terms.definition: The gate a position must pass before it can be Torque, and entry is earned three ways at once: a structural tailwind from an identifiable regime force, business survivability through stress without continuous access to capital markets, and valuation headroom large enough for a convex payoff, often five times or more. Passing earns a place, not a size.

source.ref: Part 5 — Torque: leverage on regime forces

terms.definition: A checklist, not an impression: a Ballast candidate must pass at least three of five tests covering a fortress balance sheet, diversified revenue, durable cash generation, low factor correlation, and a liquidity-resilient valuation. Yield is deliberately not on the list; income follows quality rather than qualifying it.

source.ref: Part 5 — Ballast: five tests, three required

terms.definition: The Hype exit schedule: one third of the position is sold at a fifty percent gain, another third at one hundred percent, and the remainder runs with the stop raised to breakeven. It converts a narrative trade into banked gains without pretending to know the top.

The middle layer of change governance: a threshold that may be tuned inside a documented envelope for an articulated reason, such as component weights, sizing bands, momentum thresholds, or concentration limits. Changing one adjusts the framework; changing doctrine abandons it.

The rule that every change to the rules is itself governed, by routing it to exactly one of three levels: doctrine, which cannot change without abandoning the framework; parameters, tunable within documented ranges; and overrides, temporary, documented, and time-bounded.

A state machine for stressed markets, when rising correlation and departing liquidity make positions that looked independent trade as one. The response is deliberately boring: pause new Torque adds, enforce posture limits strictly, consider trimming gross exposure by ten to twenty percent, and resume only after two calm weeks.

source.ref: Part 5 — Liquidity and correlation: throttle the regime

appearsLater.topic: Liquidity and correlation: throttle the regime

terms.definition: The heaviest CIS component at forty percent, because asymmetric upside is the objective. It scores TAM headroom, the optionality surface, catalyst density, and scarcity, each capped, summing to a 0 to 100 component score.

source.ref: Part 6 — The four CIS components; Framework in Math, component C

terms.definition: The CIS component, weighted twenty-five percent, that measures survivability under stress rather than price volatility: balance sheet, business-model fragility, factor correlation, and tail exposure. A higher score means lower fragility.

source.ref: Part 6 — The four CIS components; Framework in Math, component R

terms.definition: The CIS component, weighted twenty-five percent, that measures fit to the current regime rather than a forecast: regime sensitivity, carry direction, and policy alignment against the Part 2 thesis. A macro read may tilt a score; it is bounded so it can never determine one.

source.ref: Part 6 — The four CIS components; Framework in Math, component M

terms.definition: The lightest CIS component at ten percent: momentum, relative strength, and market acceptance. It carries the least weight because execution confirms quality and never dominates it.

source.ref: Part 6 — The four CIS components; Framework in Math, component E

terms.definition: How much larger the addressable market is than the company, the first and largest sub-score inside Convexity and Optionality. It is scored on a logarithmic curve capped at thirty times, so the first multiple of headroom counts for far more than the twentieth.

source.ref: Framework in Math — Convexity and optionality; Part 5 Torque eligibility

terms.definition: A sub-score inside Convexity and Optionality that prices identifiable, dated reasons for a re-rating. Each catalyst earns points from its impact, probability, independence, evidence confidence, and time decay, so several versions of the same catalyst do not count twice.

source.ref: Framework in Math — Convexity and optionality

terms.definition: The five named deductions FIS can take from one hundred: allocation, governance, dead capital, concentration, and complexity, each with its own cap. Because the caps sum to eighty, FIS can never fall below twenty, and every point lost names the rule that cost it.

The FIS reading of seventy: at or above it the portfolio holds, below it repair begins, with the attribution naming the fix. CIS reads the same four-band register, but there seventy is only the floor of the Strong band, a boundary rather than a trigger.

The ten-point signal on score movement. A CIS rise of ten points flags the position for resizing toward its larger target, a fall of ten flags a downsize, and either is paced over two to four weeks. Neither changes posture, which Part 5 governs, and neither alone forces an exit.

All CIS sub-scores are continuous values rather than bucketed tiers: a position scores 78.3, not 75 or 80. Continuity preserves the small week-over-week movement that longitudinal tracking exists to see.

The operating cadence, run Sunday evening or Monday pre-market: update CIS, calculate FIS, run the governance gates, act or deliberately hold, and log the evidence. It closes every week whether or not anything moved, which is what makes the next pass a measurement.

The four events that interrupt the weekly cadence rather than wait for it: a position moving more than five percent in one day, material news, an earnings announcement, or a tripwire condition met. Between triggers, frequency limits keep activity from passing for diligence.

Discipline includes doing nothing. A CIS or FIS change under five points is monitored, a position inside its band is not resized, and a week in which every check passed and nothing moved is the system working, not the system idle.

The failure CIS cannot see because it scores one position at a time: several high-scoring positions that move together under regime stress. Average correlation above 0.7 is flagged as a diagnostic; any penalty routes through FIS and governance, never through CIS.

A position whose score has quietly fallen while its sizing stayed put, because nobody recalculated: a thesis played out, a market compressed, catalysts exhausted. Scores stale past ninety days are flagged, and the dead-capital bucket bills them.
